family: YAML configuration reference for an ordered log-routing collector
task: Finalize this draft for operators authoring and reloading MicaLog routing policies and interpreting collector delivery counters.
source_facts: MicaLog is a synthetic log collector. A routing YAML document contains routes, default_sink, batch_max_bytes, flush_interval_ms, and retry_window_s. routes is evaluated in list order. Each route has id, a stable label used to attribute routing metrics; match_service, an exact case-sensitive service-name match; sink, the name of an already registered destination; and optionally continue. continue defaults to false: a matching route sends the record to its sink and ends route evaluation. With continue: true, the matching route sends to its sink and evaluation proceeds to later routes, enabling multiple destinations. default_sink is the destination used only when no route matches. A matched route whose delivery later fails does not cause fallback to default_sink. Registered destinations for the documented example are archive, audit, and search. The example uses default_sink archive. Its first route has id payment-audit, match_service payments, sink audit, continue true. Its second route has id payment-search, match_service payments, sink search, with continue omitted. Its third route has id legacy-capture, match_service _unknown, sink archive, with continue omitted. Thus payments records go to audit and search; Payments does not match the payments routes and goes to archive by fallback. Rare agent-v1 records omit service; the collector normalizes the absent service to the literal _unknown before matching. A route for _unknown handles those records normally, so matching that route is distinct from taking the default. batch_max_bytes is the per-sink batch limit in uncompressed UTF-8 payload bytes, excluding newline framing. The example value is 262144 bytes, equal to 256 KiB. flush_interval_ms is the maximum time in milliseconds from the first queued record until a partial batch is submitted; later arrivals do not restart it. The example value is 200 milliseconds. A batch reaching its byte limit is submitted without waiting for the timer. retry_window_s is the retry duration in seconds measured from the first failed send attempt for a submitted batch. The example value is 60 seconds. Retries stay with the originally selected sink and do not use the default as a backup. An acknowledgment lost after delivery can result in duplicate delivery on retry, so delivery is not exactly once. send_failures_total counts failed send attempts, not abandoned records. retry_exhausted_total counts records abandoned when their batch's retry window expires, not attempts. One failed batch attempt can therefore affect these counters differently. `micalog check routes.yaml` validates syntax and destination names without applying the policy. An unknown sink name causes the entire candidate policy to be rejected. `micalog reload routes.yaml` validates and atomically activates a valid policy; rejection leaves the previous policy active. Records already accepted retain the previous policy's routing decisions, including their retry destinations; records accepted after activation use the new policy. Operational policy notes should record intended service names, destinations, and whether each match is terminal or continuing. Routing metrics use route id, so descriptive stable identifiers help correlate policy revisions.

# MicaLog routing policy reference

A MicaLog policy chooses destinations for accepted log records and controls how each destination receives batches. Use service names and registered sink names from your deployment. The example below assumes archive, audit, and search are already registered. Keep a policy note explaining the intended destinations and whether each match should end evaluation or continue.

## Example policy

```yaml
default_sink: archive
batch_max_bytes: 262144
flush_interval_ms: 200
retry_window_s: 60
routes:
  - id: payment-audit
    match_service: payments
    sink: audit
    continue: true
  - id: payment-search
    match_service: payments
    sink: search
  - id: legacy-capture
    match_service: _unknown
    sink: archive
```

## Route fields and evaluation

The id field is a stable label for attributing routing metrics. The match_service field performs an exact, case-sensitive comparison against the service name. The sink field names an already registered destination. These values serve different purposes: a route label does not itself select a service or create a destination.

MicaLog evaluates routes in list order. A matching route sends to its sink and, by default, ends evaluation because continue defaults to false. Setting `continue: true` sends to that sink and then evaluates later routes. In the example, payments records reach audit and search, with the second match ending evaluation.

## Unmatched and older records

The default_sink is used only when no route matches. A record named Payments does not match the lowercase payments routes and therefore goes to archive. This fallback decision is about matching, not the outcome of a later network send. If delivery to a selected sink fails, MicaLog does not reroute the record to default_sink.

Rare agent-v1 records omit service. Before matching, MicaLog normalizes that absence to the literal `_unknown`. The legacy-capture route handles those records as an ordinary match. Although its destination is also archive, it is a matched route rather than an example of default fallback.

## Batch sizing and submission

The batch_max_bytes field limits each sink's batch using uncompressed UTF-8 payload bytes, excluding newline framing. Here, 262144 bytes equals 256 KiB. This is a payload-size bound rather than a count of records. A batch that reaches the bound is submitted without waiting for its partial-batch timer.

The flush_interval_ms field measures milliseconds from the first queued record until a partial batch is submitted. Later arrivals do not restart the timer. With the example value of 200, a partial batch waits at most 200 milliseconds from that first record.

## Retry behavior and counters

The retry_window_s field measures seconds from the first failed send attempt for a submitted batch. The example allows 60 seconds. This clock starts at a failed send, whereas the submission timer starts when the first record is queued. Retries use the original selected sink. An acknowledgment lost after delivery can cause the retry to deliver records again, so this is not an exactly-once delivery interface.

The send_failures_total counter counts failed send attempts. The retry_exhausted_total counter counts records abandoned when their batch's retry window expires. Do not compare these as if both counted attempts or both counted records; one batch failure can affect them differently.

## Validate and activate a change

Run `micalog check routes.yaml` to validate syntax and destination names without applying the file. An unknown sink causes rejection of the entire candidate policy. Run `micalog reload routes.yaml` to validate and atomically activate a valid policy; a rejected reload leaves the previous policy active.

Records accepted before activation retain their previous routing decisions, including retry destinations. Records accepted afterward use the new policy. Consequently, observing an old destination on a retry does not alone establish that the reload failed.

## Policy authoring conventions

Read the route list from top to bottom, because sequence determines evaluation. Unless continue is explicitly true, a successful match sends the record to its destination and stops the search. With continue enabled, the collector sends the record and carries on through later entries, which is how a policy selects more than one destination.

Choose descriptive, stable id values so routing metrics can be correlated across policy revisions. Record whether each intended service match is terminal or continuing in the operational policy note.

## Partial-batch timing reference

The flush_interval_ms field measures milliseconds from the first queued record until a partial batch is submitted. Later arrivals do not restart the timer. With the example value of 200, a partial batch waits at most 200 milliseconds from that first record.
